pageOrientation: simulation-first in sequence, interface-heavy in composition

categories.label: First interaction
categories.evidence: Zero mandatory theory and zero prerequisite clicks, but the actual diagram starts below the initial viewport and the mobile pressure slider begins at 2511 px.

categories.label: Visual dominance
categories.evidence: The visual stage is first, but the desktop hydraulic diagram is 312 by 144 px and occupies 18.2 percent of its canvas while controls and panels dominate.

categories.label: Cause and effect
categories.evidence: Pressure and diameter update checked area/force results, simulation state, readings, summary, vector, equations, and challenge without a second calculation path.

categories.label: Engineering honesty
categories.evidence: Flow, ratings, vector scale, piston motion, and machine-capacity limits are disclosed; playback speed, frame, and load motion still imply dynamics absent from the model.

categories.label: Calculation integration
categories.evidence: Engineering-core supplies SI results and Live Equation exposes substitutions, steps, units, assumptions, and equation IDs; display-unit and spatial connection need refinement.

categories.label: Challenge quality
categories.evidence: The 15 kN condition, margin, and idealised feedback are clear, but success is binary, has no intentional submission, and teaches no real trade-off.

categories.label: Real-world connection
categories.evidence: The original excavator visual is relevant, concise, source-linked, and appropriately bounded, but remains static context rather than transfer practice.

categories.label: Mobile experience
categories.evidence: No overflow and usable input widths, but the page is 12297 px tall, the label-rich SVG is scaled to 257 px, and controls begin after extensive scrolling.

categories.label: Accessibility
categories.evidence: Keyboard, numeric alternatives, descriptions, reduced motion, status text, and zoom are strong; the pressure slider is focus stop 21 and state changes are not automatically announced.

categories.label: Performance
categories.evidence: The route-specific client code is 21.3 KB gzip with simple SVG and no new renderer dependency; field, low-end-device, long-task, and React commit data are missing.

verifiedCauseEffect.action: Pressure changed from 5 MPa to 10 MPa at 50 mm diameter
verifiedCauseEffect.result: Force changed from 9817.5 N to 19635 N and the pressure control pair, measurement, state summary, scene label, vector, and challenge remained synchronized.

verifiedCauseEffect.action: Diameter changed from 50 mm to 100 mm at 10 MPa
verifiedCauseEffect.result: Area changed from 0.0019635 m2 to 0.00785398 m2 and force changed to 78539.8 N, consistent with the squared-diameter relationship.

criticalFindings: The actual engineering diagram is not present in the first viewport at either tested size.
The mobile lesson is stacked rather than recomposed and delays primary inputs until 2511 px.
The hydraulic diagram is too small for its embedded labels and occupies only 18.2 percent of the desktop canvas.
Play, speed, frame, and load motion imply time dynamics absent from the pressure-area model.
Primary input changes have a text summary but no concise live announcement.
Challenge feedback, Deep Dive limitations, and source references are duplicated.
The route uses a hydraulic-slug conditional and custom feature component rather than a simulation-ID experience registry.
strengths: Pure engineering-core SI calculations drive every technical result.
The lesson requires no theory before interaction.
Flow, ratings, dynamics, faults, and real-machine limitations are honestly bounded.
Formal assessment remains authenticated and server scored.
The lesson retains honest internal and Engineering review required status.
Route-scoped SVG implementation passes the pilot bundle budget.
auditLimitations: No field time-to-interactive or Core Web Vitals data was available.
No named independent engineering, educational, safety, or assistive-technology reviewer participated.
The dark appearance was visually inspected; automated coverage supplied broader contrast evidence.
Fault-state visual language could not be audited because the pilot intentionally enables no reviewed fault.
